Design review 04 · Bloom 2 · 6 Oct 2026Exploration · H13 unedited · Field by default, Night on the toggle

CONTROL in Bloom.

A redraw of CONTROL's look after one motion loop: Bloom, an inflated flower whose colour flows through it every 7 seconds. This sheet borrows the loop's system, not its flower: a cool field that is the blue family turned down, three softened primaries that only meet through cream or navy, inflated forms shaded with navy instead of grey, and every loop a power of two of 7 seconds. Field is the default. Night is the same system with the lights off, on a plain near-black grey.

Bloom 2 moves the colour out of the lamps and into a row of flowing beads beside each session's lamp: blue working, red needs you, amber failed, green done. The lamps keep their motion and shape, in ink. The pearls and ramps that stayed on the showcase now sit inside the app, and one section tries a centre without a terminal.

Reply with

The B numbers from the H13 delta you accept and your Q answers, for example: B1–B13 yes, B19–B23 yes, Q1 beat, Q12 flip.

The H13 delta, B1–B25 and Q1–Q12

Field | Night switches the theme through its bridge. Regrade | Rounded keeps the retired rounded face one click away for comparison. Pause, ¼× and ½× hold or slow every loop on the page together, so transitions can be judged. Still shows exactly what Reduce motion shows: every bar holds a pose that still reads its state.

Changes

  • State colour lives in one place: each session's bead bar, the state's colour as one smooth ramp inside its own family, flowing through a row of beads on the clock. It takes a sixth of the row at the right, just before the lamp, and a quarter in the menu-bar panel; working and Background share it. The session in focus gets the one continuous bar, at the top. working needs you failed done
  • Lamps carry no hue. Each state keeps its own motion and shape in ink, so the lamp says how urgent and the bar says which state. In rows and the menu-bar panel the lamp is 15 px, the row's end cap.
  • Each row's second line carries Claude's spark, a small context line with its %, the tokens the chat has spent, and the age.
  • Usage, 5H and 7D, is a thin line in plain ink: no hue and no beads.
  • Pearls in the app: the bead material at 8–20 px for group identity, tallies and counts.
  • Field on the reel's own #D6DEEE is the default. Night is one neutral grey: the field #2F2E2E, wells #1B1A1A and inputs #242323 below it. Its one blue-black is only ever shading.
  • Soft forms: radius, inflated controls, no hairlines. Motion on one clock: 1.75, 3.5, 7 and 14 s, phase-locked across the window.
  • Neue Regrade for the chrome; Plex stays for everything you could paste into a shell.
  • One idea to try: a centre without a terminal. The session reads as a conversation, and the terminal is one tab away.

Stays

  • The work is the hero and the chrome stays calm, whether the centre is the terminal or the conversation.
  • Only arm red means needs you; danger means destructive. Failed is amber, well clear of arm.
  • State reads by shape first, then motion, then colour.
  • Reduce motion stills every loop, the bars included.
  • The menu-bar icon is a still template image.
  • CONTROL never presses Enter for you and never posts a banner.
02

Colour

A neutral night, a cool field, and state colour that flows. Every number computed in OKLCH.

Bloom's palette is three softened primaries, a warm cream and a cool navy. CONTROL sets them on two grounds: Field, the reel's own cool #D6DEEE and the default, and Night, a plain near-black grey whose wells and inputs step down in the same grey. State colour then has two homes: a bead bar on each session's row, its colour flowing through the beads inside one family, and pearls, for identity and for tallies. The lamp at the end of the bar keeps no hue at all, only its shape and its motion. Arm stays the one signal red, and failed leaves the reds for amber-yellow.

C1What the reel measures as

Every colour here was measured from the reel's 60 frames, one every 0.7 s, and converted to OKLCH. Frame 049 at 34.3 s is the cleanest. The reel is an Instagram upload, so the blocky patches in busier frames are video compression: an artefact, not part of the look.

bloom.md §1

Averages, not plateaus

These are k-means centres, so each is an average of what it covers. The crimson plateau is really #DC0042. The true navy floor is #0A1535: #262B5B mixes navy with cobalt. The plateau cream #ECD6C6 sits at the field's own lightness, L 0.890 against 0.899: the field's warm twin.

The tokens keep the k-means values anyway: every contrast and colour-blind proof in this section was computed on them.

C2Rest, then break

The reel doesn't flow evenly. It rests on one family, then breaks into stripes on its way to the next. Rest takes about 40 % of the cycle and the break about 60 %. Cream makes the bright breaks; navy makes the one dark break, where blue turns to red. The hero ramp keeps that rhythm. A state bar keeps only the rest: it never leaves its family, so it has nothing to break into.

Theory 7.6

Rest versus transition

Bloom rests on one hue, with one family holding 55–75 % of the object; in the stripes between rests no family holds more than 31–43 %.

A state bar is a rest that never ends. It blends inside one family, base to light, back to base, down to deep and back, about a third of a tile nearest each step, with no bridge in it, so it flows without a single band. The window around it stays field and ink. When something needs you, every hero ramp gives way and the needs-you bar is the only arm on screen.

C3A softened triad, and one more hue

Bloom's three hues are RGB, softened. On OKLab's colour plane, hue is the angle and chroma the distance from grey at the centre. The base steps sit 127.4°, 136.5° and 96.1° apart: near sRGB's primaries, never on them. The one place they come close to arm is red, so that is where CONTROL draws a moat. Failed gets a hue of its own, amber-yellow, a long way out of it.

Theory 7.1

Softened primaries as a triad

Three hues about 120° apart are as far apart as three colours can be, so the families never compete for one meaning. Bloom's red is turned 24° toward pink, and each base step stops short of the gamut wall, tone-mapped toward cream above.

That headroom is the signal channel. Arm is the one colour at the wall, and past it on a P3 display.

§11.2

A fourth hue, for one job

Theory 7.10

Why OKLCH

Its lightness is close to perceptually even, so a plateau really is one lightness. Its hue holds as chroma changes (HSL's blue drifts purple), so a family keeps its identity from wash to deep. And a blend in OKLab skips sRGB's dark, dull middle: cobalt to crimson meets at L 0.490 in sRGB and 0.541 in OKLab.

C4Two grounds, two ladders

Field keeps the reel's own cool field. Night is new: a plain near-black grey, #2F2E2E, at chroma 0.001, so nothing on it has to fight a blue cast. Chrome steps up from it in the same grey, and everything sunk steps down in it too: inputs and tracks to #242323, the wells, where the terminal, the chat, code and diffs live, to #1B1A1A. Bloom 2's first cut kept v1's navy, #131528, for the wells; against the grey it read as a blue cast, so it went. The one blue-black left, #060714, is shading: shadows and inset gradients, never a fill. The inks climb from cool to cream-warm. Nothing is pure black or white.

Theory 7.2

Cream and navy as value poles, grey in between

Every Bloom hue sits between two poles: cream above at L 0.837, navy below at 0.312. Night now puts a neutral ground between them. Chrome rises from it in grey (raised 1.14, overlay 1.33, seam 1.63) and everything sunk falls in the same grey (sunken 1.16, the well 1.28), in even steps of about 0.04 L. Occlusion, 1.48, is only ever a shadow. Only selection rises in blue, so a selected row still reads as chosen.

Cream is still today's working ink in disguise: the two share OKLab L 0.837 and differ by ΔE 0.026, about one just-noticeable difference. It works as the light bridge in the hero ramp, and in the wipe when a session changes state; a state bar itself never shows it.

Theory 7.4

A cool field pushes; a neutral one doesn't

on #D6DEEEon #2F2E2E

Both squares are the same cream. A surround pushes what it holds toward its own complement: Field's field sits at h 264.4, so everything on it leans toward h 84.4, yellow. Cream reads creamier, warm hues advance and blues recede. It is also why Field's failed bar reads at all: amber sits on the field's complement.

Night's field has no hue to push, C 0.001, so the colours on it read as themselves. That is what you asked of it.

Theory 7.8

The rim, at 0.60 on the grey

Bloom shades a bead's lower edge toward navy. On a dark ground that edge disappears, so a cream rim gives the silhouette back. On #2F2E2E the old 0.45 rim falls to 2.31–2.69:1 against the field.

At 0.60 it reaches 3.44–3.80:1 on the field, 3.01–3.33:1 on raised and 4.41–4.87:1 in the well: the smallest mix that clears 3:1 everywhere. Field keeps 0.30, 3.99–4.69:1. The material itself is Form F3.

C5Families, and the saturation back

Rose, green, blue and lilac are the chrome families: diff washes, TRACE kinds, focus, links. Amber is new and has one job, failed. The state bars take their own, brighter steps of blue, green and lilac, plus amber, and the chart shows how close each comes to sRGB's wall: near it, never at it. Arm alone goes past.

§7 rule 3

Near the wall, never at it

Theory 7.7

Helmholtz–Kohlrausch

Saturated colours look brighter than their luminance. Arm measures L* 57.7 but reads as L** 70.1, about 12 units brighter, which is why it glows without being the lightest thing on screen: cream is L* 80.7, L** 81.4.

So equal OKLab L is not equal brightness, and the chrome families' base steps are re-solved to one L**.

It also means arm's contrast numbers are a floor, not its strength.

§3.1, §11.1

Blue binds at the light end

At L 0.80, sRGB allows only C 0.101 at h 272 (P3 allows 0.110). Night's light steps are lifted to L 0.825–0.835 so accent text keeps the label tier on every Night surface, and up there blue-light holds C 0.082.

C6The ramp

The signature ramp is Bloom's nine stops held on plateaus, with transitions 3 % wide, so each hue shows at its true chroma for most of its length. It moves one full period every 7 s, linear, and its two ends are the same colour, so the join never shows. It lives only in hero places. Next to state, the safe ramp takes over. Bloom 2 gives the sage plateau back some of its chroma.

Theory 7.11

Isoluminant drift, not a flash

That is why the safe ramp can live anywhere near state without ever flashing. D's needs-you blink swung luminance 4.52:1; it retires, and Bloom's needs-you never dims.

§11.5

Where it comes closest to arm

C7Bridges, not blends

Between two families Bloom never blends. It holds each hue, then crosses a separator: cream between hues of similar lightness, navy where the darkest blue wraps round to the darkest red. Each pair of families has exactly one bridge. A state bar never crosses families: it stays inside one, so it blends smoothly, and the bridges are kept for the crossings, the hero ramp and the wipe when a session changes state.

Theory 7.3

Plateau and band

A straight blend between distant hues cuts across the middle of the colour plane, through grey. Coral to sage bottoms out in a dirty salmon inside arm's arc; grass to periwinkle in grey-teal; cobalt to crimson in purple.

Bloom never shows those midpoints. The eye reads a separator as light or shadow, a deliberate event, and a muddy midpoint as dirt.

§4, §11.3

Inside one family, a blend

A bar's tile is one smooth wave: base, up to light, back to base, down to deep, back to base, about a third of it nearest each step. Needs-you has no light step of its own, so it swings between arm and arm-deep, half each. Nothing in a bar is cream, navy or wine, and nothing holds still on a plateau.

So nothing reads as a band. The steepest 2 px step in any row's bar is ΔE 0.0125 in Field and 0.0124 in Night, against 0.236 and 0.210 at Bloom 2's first cut, at its bridges. The light range inside a bar falls from 6.72–10.01:1 to 1.26–2.60:1: the bar is calm, and its tempo carries urgency.

C8State lives in the bar

Bloom 2 splits the job in two. The lamp says how a session behaves, by shape and motion, in ink. The bead bar beside it says which state it is in, by colour: blue working, red needs you, amber failed, green done, lilac choose on return. Quiet states hold still. Every bar flows on the page's clock at its state's tempo, and every bar of one state shares one phase, so rows never chase each other.

§7, replacing theory 7.5's count

Saturation by area, not by count

The reel is 77 / 16 / 6: field, hues, separators. v1 allowed one saturated element per view; Bloom 2 allows saturated colour anywhere it stays small.

  1. Area. Bars are 5 px beads in rows and a 6 px line for the one session in focus; pearls are 20 px or less. Nothing chromatic is a surface, a panel or text.
  2. Ceiling. Every bar, pearl and accent stays at C 0.181 or less and under 96 % of its sRGB ceiling. Arm alone reaches C 0.225.
  3. Tempo. Needs-you alone at 1.75 s.
  4. One continuous bar per view. Lists use bead bars, or three-bead tips.
  5. Pre-emption stays. While a needs-you is lit, hero ramps turn safe; bars keep their colours.

C9Arm stays the only signal red

A saturated Bloom red at mid lightness is, by construction, close to arm. Unmitigated, Bloom's crimson is ΔE 0.117 from it, red base 0.101 and coral 0.110: 5–6 just-noticeable differences, distinct side by side but confusable at a glance. v1 then made failed a second red. Bloom 2 moves failed out of the reds altogether, to amber-yellow, and keeps the six layers that hold every other red away.

§5.2, revised

Six layers

    C10Diffs, the Bloom pair

    H13 delta B10. H13 puts removed lines on arm's dim wash and added lines on a brighter grey, never green. Bloom sinks removed lines into a rose wash below the well and raises added lines on a sage wash above it, with the marks in each family's colour. Diffs always live in the well: in Night that is #1B1A1A, a step below the grey field, never the field itself. Below, the same T14 write both ways.

    Window W3

    Line numbers stay in the gutter

    In Field, caption ink on the rose wash measures 4.38:1, under its tier. Line numbers therefore live in the sunken gutter, never on the wash. The full matrix is C11.

    C11Contrast

    Every text token against every surface it can land on, set in its own ink on its own surface, so the matrix is also the specimen. Tiers: body 7:1 and |Lc| 75; label 4.5:1 and 60; caption 4.5:1 and 45; emphasis, 13 px and weight 600 or more, 4.5:1 and 45; disabled is exempt. Night's lighter ground cost contrast, so its inks were lifted and every tier re-proved on six surfaces, the well included.

    Theory 7.9

    Light on dark isn't symmetric

    WCAG's ratio overrates light text on dark. Night's ink-4 is 6.12:1 by WCAG but only Lc −53.9 by APCA, so Night's ladder is tuned to APCA and passes WCAG on the way. The grey ground costs Night some headroom: ink-1 is 14.79:1 in the well and 11.53:1 on the field.

    Field pays for its colour. Navy on #D6DEEE is 9.84:1 and Lc 79.9, against 13.30:1 and Lc 99.5 on white; even black would only reach Lc 86.4. So Field's body text is ink-1, the navy itself, with no lighter body grey, and its secondary text stops at ink-2.

    C12Colour-blind check

    Lamps carry no hue now, so no colour-vision deficiency can touch them: ten shapes and ten motions carry state for everyone, and the state word says it outright. The bar adds colour on top. Below, each coloured bar under the three dichromat simulations (Machado 2009, full severity), flowing in its simulated colours.

    §11.4

    State never depends on the bar

    Background shares working's bar and differs by its lamp, a ring; outside by its open beads; idle and gone by having no flow. What survives every simulation is lightness, and the bases are spread from needs-you, the darkest, to failed, the lightest.

    C13Terminal palette

    ANSI's sixteen slots, in the well where the terminal lives. Normals sit at the label plateau and brights a step further from the ground. Green slots carry green, a Bloom delta, and slot 9 is a light clay rather than arm, so a CLI's bright red never wears needs-you.

    §5.8

    Slot 9 leaves arm

    Slot 9 sits ΔE 0.199 from arm in Night and 0.164 in Field. Every Night slot reaches 6.45:1 or better in the well except slot 0; every Field slot reaches 4.47:1 or better.

    03

    Motion

    One clock: 1.75, 3.5, 7 and 14 s.

    The reel loops because every period in it is a power of two of 7 seconds. CONTROL takes the clock, not the flower: every loop runs at 1.75, 3.5, 7 or 14 s from one shared instant, so the window breathes as one object. Each session now moves in two places at once. Its lamp carries the motion, in ink. Its state bar carries the colour, flowing at the state's tempo on the same clock. Linear means work, sine means waiting, still means nothing to do.

    M1One clock

    Every loop counts from one instant: host time floored to a 14 s boundary. Host time is shared by every process on the Mac, so the main window, the menu-bar panel and any helper land on the same phase grid without talking to each other. A loop starts one 14 s cycle early, so a lamp or a bar that appears late is already in step: nothing fills in, and nothing stores a phase. One-shots never wait for the beat. A change shows on the frame it's caused; only its loop falls into step.

    M2Five curves

    Space is sine and colour is linear, as in the reel. The rule that falls out of it: linear means work, sine means waiting, still means nothing to do. Working, Background, housekeeping and the loader are linear lamps: a machine doing something. Needs-you, done, failed, choose, outside and idle are sine: a thing waiting, breathing. Gone is still.

    Every state bar is colour travel, so every bar is linear. What tells a waiting bar from a working one is its tempo, and the lamp beside it.

    M3Every lamp and bar, live and still

    Urgency is ranked by four levers, most salient first: reach (does the motion leave the lamp?), tempo, channel (scale, then travel, then fill level, then opacity) and hue. The lamp carries the first three in ink, so every eye reads state the same way, colour-blind or not. The bead bar before it adds the fourth: blue working, amber failed, green done, and red for needs-you alone.

    In a row the two sit together at the right: a run of beads a sixth of the row wide, then the lamp at the far end as its cap. Read right to left, the lamp says what's happening and the beads say it in colour. Each bar is one smooth wave inside its state's family, base to light to base to deep, so the colour flows through the beads with no band in it. Needs-you alone runs at 1.75 s; failed and done at 3.5 s; working, Background and choose at 7 s; housekeeping at 14 s. Idle, outside and gone hold still. Working and Background share one bar; the lamp tells them apart. Only the one session in focus keeps a continuous bar, at the top of the view.

    M4A sidebar on the clock

    Five rows run a script on the shared clock. Each frame is computed from where the clock is, so a scrub or a ?t= shot lands on the exact state, and a jump never plays a transition. State never waits; only position may lag, by one T/16 at most. Every bar of one state shares one phase, so the working bars here flow as one.

    M5Fire any change

    A change of state is the reel's rest → stripes → settle, played in two places at once. In the lamp, the new shape is drawn and an ink band sweeps up through it. In the bar, the old ramp is wiped off left to right by its bridge, while the new ramp is already flowing underneath, in phase since the first frame. A bar on its own never holds a bridge: it stays inside one family, so it blends. A change crosses families, so it bridges. Most changes pass through cream: a bright, ordinary change. A calm state turning into needs-you, or back, passes through navy and wine instead: the system's one dark beat, so a calm session suddenly needing you has its own drop. In a row the wipe runs under the beads, so the bridge crosses them bead by bead.

    M6A session going needs-you, end to end

    M7Panels and the selection bar

    Ambient motion says state and nothing else: here, the lamps and the state bars. One-shot motion may also answer your hand (press, hover, focus, panels, rows, theme), and it ends within 875 ms. Panels lay out once and then animate the layer: the final frame commits on the first frame, so the terminal reflows exactly once, and the panel's content slides 24 pt and fades in.

    M8ARCHIVE row actions

    M9Theme without a flash

    Crossfading every colour per element sends the window through mid-grey mush, where text and ground pass through equal lightness: an unreadable frame, then a jump. So lightness moves one way only, through the bridge. Night → Field passes through cream and only rises; Field → Night passes through navy and only falls. It is the reel's rest → bridge → rest at window scale.

    M10Signature components

    M11Core Animation recipes

    Every loop is a render-server animation, committed once on a state change. No main-thread work happens per frame: the only main-thread cost is adding or removing an animation in the transaction that applies a daemon View. Each lamp is at most 3 layers and at most 2 running animations. A state bar is one gradient layer with one running animation, a translate: in a row it slides under a still mask of beads, and the head bar slides in a clipping pill.

    M12Principles and don'ts

    04

    Form and type

    Soft forms, no hairlines, Neue Regrade for the chrome.

    Edges come from temperature and tone, not strokes. A raised thing separates from its ground by a small step in lightness and a warm lip; a sunk thing by a cool navy shadow on its top edge. Nothing is outlined, and nothing casts a grey shadow.

    F1The softness scale

    Eight radii, and each belongs to one kind of object. The smaller the thing, the tighter its corner, so a keycap still looks exact beside a pane and a row still lines up with the terminal. Anything you press or switch is a pill. The 28 px corner exists only for showcase objects on this sheet and never reaches the app.

    F2Edges without lines

    Direction D parted regions with 1 px rules and square corners. Bloom parts them with tone: the chrome is one small step lighter than the field, wells one step darker, and regions sit apart on 6 pt gutters. In Night the field, the chrome and the wells are one neutral grey: the chrome steps up from #2F2E2E, the wells step down to #1B1A1A, and nothing carries a blue cast, so the field stays out of the way of the state colours. Where two things share a tone and still need parting, a 2 pt rounded seam does it. That seam is the only line in the window.

    F3The inflated material

    Bloom shades its objects toward navy, never grey. On the light field that gives a dark silhouette for free. On Night's grey field, #2F2E2E, the navy shading lands close to the field's own value and the edge goes soft. A cream rim at the silhouette brings it back. v1's 0.45 now reaches only 2.31–2.69:1 against the field. At 0.60 it reaches 3.44–3.80:1 on the field and 3.01–3.33:1 on raised chrome, so 0.60 is not taste: it is the smallest rim that gives every silhouette the 3:1 graphics need, field and chrome alike. Inside a well it reaches 4.41–4.87:1. Field keeps 0.30, which softens its edge.

    The pearl is the same material made for chrome, at 8 to 20 px: one still element, no pseudo-element, so a sidebar of them costs nothing. It carries a group's identity beside its name, a session's state in a tally, and a count. Under 10 px it drops the lift and keeps the rim and the occlusion, so it stays crisp. A pearl never carries text, except the neutral count pearl.

    F4Two chrome faces and Plex

    Chrome is set in Neue Regrade, your pick, and content stays in Plex. Rounded (Nunito, standing in for SF Pro Rounded) stays in the first column only as the comparison it lost. Plex keeps everything you could paste into a shell. The three columns below stay fixed whatever the nav says; the nav's Regrade | Rounded toggle still swaps every chrome string on the page if you want to look again.

    F5Glyphs and the mark

    D drew its glyphs on a 16 grid with square caps and mitred joins, ORBIT's orthogonal law. Bloom keeps the grid and the paths and rounds every cap and join, so the set matches the soft forms without changing what any glyph says. Five glyphs are new, for a centre without a terminal: term, send, stop, clip and diff. A sixth, spark, is Claude's own mark: it stands in for the word claude on every session row. The stair mark gets the same treatment.

    The lamps are glyphs too, and in Bloom 2 they are ink only: shape and motion say the state, and the bead bar just before them carries the colour. Done is a tick and it holds still; failed is a cross that stumbles. The half-moon is gone: v1 set a dot in the ring's corner, and at row size that read as a crescent.

    F6Space

    05

    The window

    Main window in both themes, ARCHIVE and the diff, rows at 1:1.

    A redraw, not a reskin. The sidebar now runs the full height of the window and holds the traffic lights, so the band belongs to the session you selected: its group's pearl, its name, and under the name the one full state bar in the window, flowing over the terminal. Every row ends in its own bead bar and lamp, every group has its pearl, and usage is a plain line of ink. Lamps keep their shapes and motions and lose their colour. The terminal is still the centre, in a deep well; the next section, Without a terminal, takes it out.

    W1Field

    Field is the default. The chrome is one tone step above the field (1.11:1) and the terminal sits on the field itself, in a soft well, with navy ink at 9.84:1. Colour lives in the bars, the pearls and the live turn's rail, and inside the wells in the kind labels and the diff; everything else is the field, the chrome and ink. ORBIT-WEBSITE is selected, so its working bar runs 6 px tall and unbroken in the band, and as a row of 5 px beads in its row, both on the 7 s working period. Each bar is one smooth blend inside its own family, so its colour flows rather than steps. STATISTICS's bar is the only arm on screen and, with its lamp, the fastest thing on it: one period every 1.75 s.

    TRACE streams T14 on the shared clock: seven events between 0.9 s and 8.8 s, the turn marks done at 10 s, and the stream starts again every 14 s. Its turns hang on a rail of pearls, and the live turn's rail is the safe ramp, so it can flow right beside state.

    W2Night, on #2F2E2E

    Night's field is a plain near-black grey, #2F2E2E, with a chroma of 0.001. The chrome steps up from it in the same grey (1.14:1) and everything sunk steps down in it: the terminal, TRACE and OUTPUTS sit in #1B1A1A wells, 1.28:1 below the field, and the tabs' track, the usage track and the diff gutters in #242323, 1.16:1 below. No surface carries a hue, so nothing pulls against the blue, green and amber bars; the only blue-black left is the shading under raised things. Ink-1 is 11.53:1 on the field and 14.79:1 in the well.

    Every pearl carries a stronger cream rim in Night, mixed at 0.60: the smallest rim that gives a pearl's silhouette 3:1 on the field (3.44–3.80) and on the chrome (3.01–3.33).

    W3ARCHIVE open, with the diff

    ARCHIVE opens under the sessions: search, sort, and 412 finished sessions and chats, the count in a pearl. Three rows are selected, so the selection note has risen at the sidebar's foot, inside its own region. On the right, TRACE is in Diff mode: the same writes as one diff against HEAD, in the well. Night's well is a neutral #1B1A1A and the two washes sit either side of it: removed lines sink 0.049 below it in lightness and added lines rise 0.056 above it. In Field they move −0.037 and +0.030. Long lines wrap under their code.

    W4Rows at 1:1

    Every state and every interaction at its real size: rows 42, groups 28, worktree rows 22. Read a row from the right. The lamp is the end cap, 15 px, ink, and it only moves. Before it, a bead bar a sixth of the row wide carries the colour, flowing through its beads. The name has the rest of the first line. Needs you flows fastest, one period every 1.75 s at 68.6 px/s. Failed and done take 3.5 s at 51.4 px/s; working, background and choose 7 s at 34.3 px/s; housekeeping 14 s on the safe ramp. Outside, idle and gone hold still.

    The second line starts with Claude's spark and the state words, then any chip. Under the bar sit the context line and its share, the tokens this chat has spent, and the age, so every column lines up down the list. A needs-you row also takes a 6 % arm tint and a semibold name, and ink-1 on it is 9.89:1 in Field and 9.58:1 in Night. Working and background share one bar; the lamp tells them apart, a disc for one job and a ring for several, and the wave after the state words counts them. Outside's beads are open rings, like its lamp, and its row has no spark: it is not Claude's. Idle and gone show only the track. A folded group swaps its rows for a tally: one pearl per hidden session, each in its own session's colour. Field's amber bar is only 1.62:1 on the chrome, so it reads by hue, while the lamp's stumble and the word failed carry it for everyone.

    W5The band without the sidebar

    Hide the sidebar (⌘B) and the band takes over the session's identity: the traffic lights, the lamp, the group's pearl, the name and the full bar. It is the one place a lamp sits in the band. Pick a state: the lamp changes shape and motion, and both bars are wiped off by their bridge while the new ramp already flows underneath, in 437.5 ms, or 218.75 ms into needs you. A bar blends inside its own family; a change crosses families, so it bridges: cream, except between a calm state and needs you, where it is navy and wine. With Still on, the change dissolves in 218.75 ms instead.

    06

    Without a terminal

    A chat-first centre over Claude's real TUI. The terminal becomes a tab.

    Your wacky idea, drawn. The centre stops being a terminal and becomes the conversation: your prompt opens each turn, every read, write, error and agent sits in line as a card, and Claude's reply streams in under them. Today TRACE repeats the terminal line for line; here each thing is said once. Claude's own TUI keeps running in tmux, untouched, one click away as the terminal tab beside Browser and Git.

    It is drawn over option C of the research: a chat view over the real TUI. CONTROL's mod already runs inside every session and already sees every row the conversation keeps, and the reply as it streams; the centre is drawn from that. The composer is CONTROL's own text field, and Send pre-types into Claude's prompt box, then adds the one Enter you pressed. Nothing here is built. The last part of this section says what is still unproven.

    X1The window, chat first

    The same sessions and the same Claude turn as the window in section 05, with a different centre. The sidebar runs the full height and holds the lights, so the head of the conversation says only what the selected row doesn't: the session's path and, under it, the one full state bar in the window, a single smooth blend inside its state's family that flows on the clock. The lamp, the pearl, the name, the state and the worktree are already on that row, so they aren't repeated. In the sidebar every row carries the same colour through its beads, a sixth of the row, just before the lamp at the far right. Each turn hangs from a thread in the gutter. Your prompt sits on a soft raised pebble, in Plex, because it is exactly what you typed. Every tool call is a pearl on the thread, and Claude's reply reads in the chrome face.

    The live turn's thread carries the safe ramp, flowing, and its head is the one marble in the well. When the turn ends, both settle to cream and the session's bar wipes from blue to green, in the head and in its sidebar row together. The panel's tabs are icons: Outputs, Folder, Browser, Git and the terminal. Diff lives inside Git as a mode, Graph | Diff, the way TRACE carries Turns | Diff in the terminal window. TRACE is gone as a tab, because its rows are the conversation now, and the terminal is the small glyph at the end of the strip.

    X3Cards at 1:1

    One grammar for every kind of row, borrowed from TRACE: a pearl on the turn's thread, the kind in its TRACE colour, the path in Plex, the meta at the right, and a chevron when there is more. A write opens its diff for the live turn and folds in older ones. Consecutive reads fold to one row. A subagent is a session in its own right, so its card carries a tip, three beads in its own state's colour.

    Needs-you cards are a different object. They float up from the well on the overlay tone, because they are the one thing in the conversation that waits for you, and the session's bar and lamp turn needs-you while they wait. The first cut only shows the card and leaves the answer to Claude's dialog; the later cut lets your click send the dialog's own key.

    X4The pipe, and why not fakechat

    You named fakechat, so it was the first thing tested, and it is the wrong pipe for the centre. A channel is an MCP server that Claude Code spawns over stdio. It carries one thing in and one thing out: your message arrives as an outside event (<channel source="plugin:fakechat:fakechat" …>, not your typed turn), and only what Claude passes to the channel's reply tool comes back. fakechat's own instructions to Claude say it plainly: "Anything you want them to see must go through the reply tool — your transcript output never reaches the UI" (server.ts:63). The work, which is what you want in the centre, never crosses it.

    CONTROL already ships the pipe that does carry the work. Its mod runs inside every Claude session, and the mod API has session.append, which "fires once per row a conversation of this session keeps (a prompt, a response block, a tool result, a notice), before it is stored" (index.d.ts:4196-4207), and turn.step, which streams the response chunk by chunk (:1135-1139). That is the whole chat, live, with no file tailing.

    X5Said once

    Where every fact lives today, in direction D's terminal, TRACE and footer, and where it lives with the conversation in the centre. TRACE (F27) is mapped, not built (docs/CHECKLIST.md:71), so retiring it as a tab costs nothing already shipped.

    X6What it does to the hard rules

    One amendment, and it is small: H1 gains a sentence for Send. Everything else the spec guards keeps working as it does today, because the TUI, tmux and the mod's two promises are untouched.

    X7Not proven yet

    These decide how far the drawing above can go. None is a design decision; each needs a test or your call.

    07

    Around the window

    Menu bar, lock, icon, sheets and notes, with pearls and state bars inside them.

    The menu-bar icon stays a still template image: state by shape. The panel under it gets pearls and bead bars: one pearl per session in its header, and on every row a short bar of beads with the colour flowing through them, just before the lamp. The lock screen is the one CONTROL screen where nothing needs you, so it is the one place the whole ramp is allowed to move.

    A1Menu-bar icon

    macOS draws a template image in one ink and recolours it for each bar, so the icon carries no colour, and it carries no motion either. The stair holds every state by shape alone: the apex step fills for working, a check in the right shoulder marks done, and the whole canvas reverses for needs you. Bloom changes two things. Strokes take round caps and round joins, like the mark. And done's filled corner square becomes a check, because Bloom 2 drops every corner mark for done: a square or dot in a corner was the half-moon's grammar.

    A2The menu-bar panel

    The panel is 360 wide and floats, so it takes the overlay tone, the navy float shadow and a lip of light on its top edge. Its header line is three pearl tallies, one pearl per session in that session's own state colour, each with its count beside it: the mix reads at a glance, and the number is there without a hover. Every row is the sidebar's row at the panel's width: the name on the first line, then a bead bar a quarter of the panel wide, then the lamp at the far right as its end cap, 15 px. The second line holds Claude's spark and the state words, then the context line, the tokens the chat has spent and the age. The session that needs you keeps its tint and takes a third line for Go to tab. Lamps and bars run on the window's clock, so the needs-you beads here flow in step with the ones in the sidebar.

    A3The lock screen

    A full lock is a commitment: no early unlock. It is also the one CONTROL screen where nothing needs you, so it is the one place the whole ramp may move. The shut stair is 30 beads with the full ramp laid once around it. It turns once every 14 s, the slowest loop in the app, and each bead breathes on the same 14 s as the colour passes through it. Nothing else moves.

    When a session needs you, only that session opens. The window comes to the front without key focus, its band carries the lamp, the note and the session's full state bar, and the lock mark drops to the safe ramp, so the needs-you bar is the only arm in view.

    A4App icon

    The icon is the only other place the full ramp appears, and it does not move. The bead stair rides 3 % of the body above centre on Night's grey field, #2F2E2E, where the plateaus read cleanly against no hue at all; at 64 and 32 px the beads close up into one coloured stair.

    A5Sheets and the ⌘K finder

    Sheets float at radius 20 with the navy float shadow. Fields and wells sink, buttons are pills, and the selected segment slides. One primary per sheet, in ink. Danger text appears once, on Archive anyway?, because archiving ends a session mid-turn. The lock sheet's no-early-unlock sentence is a promise, not a danger, so it stays in ink.

    A6Notes, not toasts

    A7Empty states

This round makes every state bar a bead bar at the right of its row, blends each bar inside its own family, draws usage as a plain ink line and takes the last blue-black out of Night's surfaces.
